## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [App](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html)
- A fully assembled app, ready to serve its protocol.
- [AppBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.AppBuilder.html)
- Assembles an `App`
- [AppRegistry](https://docs.rs/struct.AppRegistry.html)
- Holds the *agnostic*component, provider, and config-binding descriptors of an app — declarations only. Runtime instances live in the`ScopeContainer`
- [AppRuntime](https://docs.rs/struct.AppRuntime.html)
- Everything a protocol needs to drive requests through DI, cheaply cloneable.
- [Boxed](https://docs.rs/struct.BoxedComponent.html)- Component
- A type-erased instantiated component.
- [Cfg](https://docs.rs/struct.Cfg.html)
- An injected configuration value, bound from a property path.
- [CfgNext](https://docs.rs/struct.CfgNext.html)
- A **proposed**configuration value handed to a`#[hook(ConfigReload)]`method during a reload, before it is committed. Read-only; derefs to`T`. If every hook accepts the proposal the value is committed into its`Cfg<T>`
- [Changed](https://docs.rs/struct.ChangedBinding.html)- Binding
- One binding changed by a reload.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentConstructionContext.html)- Construction - Context
- Context passed to a component factory during construction.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Static metadata describing a component and how to construct it.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentFactoryDescriptor.html)- Factory - Descriptor
- One way to construct a component, carrying the dependencies *that constructor*needs (zero or many).
- [Component](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentHookReport.html)- Hook - Report
- One component’s config-reload hook outcome.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentRegistry.html)- Registry
- Holds the component and provider *descriptors*of an application — declarations only. Runtime instances live in the`ScopeContainer`
- [Component](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentSource.html)- Source
- A `Resolver``ScopeContainer`
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigBinding.html)- Binding
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigBindingDescriptor.html)- Binding - Descriptor
- The link-time form of a `ConfigBinding``#[config(path = "..")]`so it is picked up by`ConfigManager::auto_discover``ConfigManager::with_config``Descriptor<ConfigBindingDescriptor>`.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigManager.html)- Manager
- The merged configuration tree, owning the format it was read in.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigReload.html)- Reload
- The config-reload hook kind: a `#[hook(ConfigReload)]`method runs when a config it targets is reloaded, receiving the proposed value(s) as`CfgNext<T>``HookOutcome`
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigReloadReport.html)- Reload - Report
- The outcome of a successful reload.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigReloader.html)- Reloader
- A cheap, cloneable, injectable handle that re-reads configuration on demand.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigStore.html)- Store
- A `Resolver``Cfg<T>`resolves through`ctx.get_resolver::<ConfigStore>()`rather than the component container. Bindings are deduped per`(type, path)`upstream, so the inner path map holds exactly one seed per path.
- [Dependency](https://docs.rs/struct.DependencyDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Declares that a component requires another component (or a config value).
- [Dir](https://docs.rs/struct.Dir.html)
- A resolved application directory of kind `K`, injectable by value.
- [Directories](https://docs.rs/struct.DirectoriesManager.html)- Manager
- Resolves and hands out the application’s `Dir<K>`
- [Directories](https://docs.rs/struct.DirectoriesResolver.html)- Resolver
- A `config::Resolver``@`directory namespace.
- [Dynamic](https://docs.rs/struct.Dynamic.html)
- Field wrapper marking a dependency as **runtime-provided**.
- [Flags](https://docs.rs/struct.Flags.html)
- Combinable control-flow flags carried in the flags section of a
`StatusCode`
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Static metadata for one hook, registered into its type’s `{Type}Hooks`slice.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookManager.html)- Manager
- Runs hooks of a kind against the live component instances.
- [Incoming](https://docs.rs/struct.IncomingCall.html)- Call
- An inbound RPC call received from the transport layer.
- [Live](https://docs.rs/struct.Live.html)
- A shared, swappable cell holding the current `Arc<T>`instance — the interior mutability primitive behind`Dep<T>``Cfg<T>`in the config layer).
- [LiveRef](https://docs.rs/struct.LiveRef.html)
- A guard pinning one generation of a `Live<T>``T`. Holding it keeps observing the generation current when`get``Live`, discouraging holding it across a long await (which would pin the old instance and delay a reload). Returned by both`Dep<T>``Cfg<T>`.
- [Logging](https://docs.rs/struct.LoggingConfig.html)- Config
- Tracing/logging settings consumed by the `init_tracing`helper, bound from a config subtree and injected as`Cfg<LoggingConfig>`
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryCall.html)- Call
- A client-side handle to one in-flight call, covering all four kinds: send inbound items (client/bidi), receive server events, and cancel.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryClient.html)- Client
- The client side of an in-memory transport. Primarily used in tests.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryConnection.html)- Connection
- A logical in-memory connection. Yielded by `MemoryTransport::accept`.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryConnectionHandle.html)- Connection - Handle
- A handle representing one logical connection on the client side. Dropped when the client is done with the connection.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryResponder.html)- Responder
- Sends responses back through the call’s event channel (unary or streaming).
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryTransport.html)- Transport
- The daemon side of an in-memory transport. Yields one `MemoryConnection`per`MemoryClient::connect`call.
- [Peer](https://docs.rs/struct.PeerInfo.html)- Info
- Transport-level information about the remote peer.
- [Provider](https://docs.rs/struct.ProviderDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Declares that a component **provides**a trait, so it can be injected as a single`Arc<dyn Trait>`(the primary or sole provider), or collected into a`Vec<Arc<dyn Trait>>`/`HashMap<String, Arc<dyn Trait>>`of all providers.
- [Reload](https://docs.rs/struct.ReloadProposal.html)- Proposal
- The proposed configuration handed to config-reload hooks: the staged value of every
binding (changed bindings hold their newly-deserialized value, unchanged bindings hold
their current value), so a hook’s `CfgNext<T>`
- [Reload](https://docs.rs/struct.ReloadTriggers.html)- Triggers
- Which automatic reload triggers a `ConfigManager``ConfigReloader::reload``serve`/`run`and spawns the matching background tasks.
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolverSet.html)- Set
- A type-keyed bag of `Resolver``ResolverCtx`
- [Scope](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)- Container
- One scope’s constructed instances, layered over an optional parent scope.
- [Server](https://docs.rs/struct.ServerConfig.html)- Config
- Network binding settings for a daemon’s transport, bound from a config subtree
and injected as `Cfg<ServerConfig>`
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.Shutdown.html)
- Fired once when the daemon begins a graceful shutdown (the serve/run loop has stopped).
Errors from a `#[hook(Shutdown)]`are logged; shutdown proceeds regardless.
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.ShutdownHandle.html)- Handle
- A cloneable handle for triggering graceful shutdown from any task.
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.ShutdownSignal.html)- Signal
- Coordinates graceful daemon shutdown across all tasks in the process.
- [Startup](https://docs.rs/struct.Startup.html)
- Fired once after the daemon is built and before it begins serving. An `Err`from any`#[hook(Startup)]`aborts startup — the daemon does not begin accepting work.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/struct.StatusCode.html)- Code
- A structured status code carried on every error response.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamDecodeError.html)- Decode - Error
- A failure decoding a wire frame back into a stream item.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamEncodeError.html)- Encode - Error
- A failure encoding a stream item into a wire frame. Carries the `StatusCode`and body the terminating`StreamError`frame will report, mirroring the handler-side error currency so a custom codec can classify its own failures.
- [TcpTransport](https://docs.rs/struct.TcpTransport.html)
- TCP transport. Each accepted connection handles calls sequentially.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Static metadata describing a Rust type, safe to embed in `'static`descriptors.
- [Unix](https://docs.rs/struct.UnixTransport.html)- Transport
- Unix socket transport. Removes the socket file on drop.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/struct.WireRequest.html)- Request
- The request half of the wire protocol, also the opening frame of a stream.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/struct.WireResponse.html)- Response
- The response half of the wire protocol.
- [Wiring](https://docs.rs/struct.Wiring.html)
- The crate-wide anchor that each component’s `Provide`impl attaches to. A dependency assertion is the bound`Wiring: Provide<Dep>`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.CallResult.html)- Result
- Success or failure of an RPC call at the transport layer.
- [Cardinality](https://docs.rs/enum.Cardinality.html)
- Cardinality of a dependency edge: how many values satisfy it.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigError.html)- Error
- Errors from loading, merging, and binding configuration.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigReloadError.html)- Reload - Error
- Errors from a configuration reload. On any error the live values are left untouched — a reload commits only when every changed binding re-binds and every affected hook accepts.
- [Default](https://docs.rs/enum.DefaultSpec.html)- Spec
- The shape of a config type’s field defaults, emitted by the `#[config]`macro and consumed by the merge step.
- [DiError](https://docs.rs/enum.DiError.html)
- The DI layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated
**factory**code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`
- [EnumTag](https://docs.rs/enum.EnumTag.html)
- How an enum is tagged, so the merge can synthesize the same shape serde deserializes.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/enum.HookError.html)- Error
- The hook layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated hook
code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`*domain*outcome (e.g. whether a config reload is accepted) is its`HookKind::Output`
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/enum.HookOutcome.html)- Outcome
- What a `#[hook(ConfigReload)]`hook reports back.`Err`from the hook aborts the reload; these variants all mean the proposal was accepted.
- [Predefined](https://docs.rs/enum.PredefinedCode.html)- Code
- The framework-owned category occupying the predefined section of a
`StatusCode`
- [Server](https://docs.rs/enum.ServerEvent.html)- Event
- A server→client event for one call. Unary calls produce a single
`Response`; streaming calls produce`Item`s terminated by`End`or`Error`.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/enum.WireMessage.html)- Message
- Top-level wire message. Every frame on the wire is one of these.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/enum.WireOutcome.html)- Outcome
- Success or failure at the wire level.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [COMPONENTS](https://docs.rs/static.COMPONENTS.html)
- Link-time registry of every discovered `ComponentDescriptor`
- [CONFIG_](https://docs.rs/static.CONFIG_BINDINGS.html)- BINDINGS
- Link-time registry of every auto-registered config binding (a `#[config(path = "..")]`type), collected by`ConfigManager::auto_discover`
- [PROVIDERS](https://docs.rs/static.PROVIDERS.html)
- Link-time registry of every discovered `ProviderDescriptor``provide = dyn Trait`). See`COMPONENTS`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.Component.html)
- Metadata trait for types registerable as components.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.ComponentFactories.html)- Factories
- A component type’s own construction factories.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.ComponentHooks.html)- Hooks
- A component type’s own hooks.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.ConfigDefaults.html)- Defaults
- Runtime, object-safe access to a config type’s `DefaultSpec`
- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.ConfigProperties.html)- Properties
- A struct bindable from a configuration subtree, injectable as `Cfg<Self>`
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/trait.Connection.html)
- A live session between the daemon and one remote peer.
- [Container](https://docs.rs/trait.ContainerConfigExt.html)- Config - Ext
- Ad-hoc config access from a built container: the relocated `.config()`accessor.
- [Descriptor](https://docs.rs/trait.Descriptor.html)
- Connects a type to a static descriptor of kind `D`, enabling type-to-descriptor lookups where the type is known but its link-time descriptor would otherwise only be reachable through a slice.
- [DirKind](https://docs.rs/trait.DirKind.html)
- A kind of application directory. Implemented by the marker types and used by
`DirectoriesManager``Dir<Self>`
- [Factory](https://docs.rs/trait.Factory.html)
- An async factory function whose parameters are all `FromContainer``FactoryOutput``Args`is the parameter-tuple marker that selects the arity impl.
- [Factory](https://docs.rs/trait.FactoryOutput.html)- Output
- What a factory function may return: the component itself, or a `Result`of it.
- [From](https://docs.rs/trait.FromContainer.html)- Container
- A single factory parameter, resolvable from the construction context, that reports the dependency edge it represents.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/trait.HookKind.html)- Kind
- A kind of hook: the event a `#[hook(Kind)]`method reacts to.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/trait.HookParam.html)- Param
- A parameter a `#[hook(K)]`method may take: an input of kind`K`, extracted from the kind’s context — never a component dependency (those come through`&self`).
- [Injectable](https://docs.rs/trait.Injectable.html)
- How a resolved dependency is stored in, and handed out of, the container.
- [Plugin](https://docs.rs/trait.Plugin.html)
- A general extension unit applied to an app while it is built.
- [Protocol](https://docs.rs/trait.Protocol.html)
- A pluggable serve/dispatch layer over the app’s DI runtime. There is exactly one
active protocol per `App`.
- [Protocol](https://docs.rs/trait.ProtocolPlugin.html)- Plugin
- A `Plugin``Protocol``App`is built around exactly one of these.
- [Provide](https://docs.rs/trait.Provide.html)
- Compile-time dependency marker: `Wiring: Provide<T>`holds when some component in scope provides`T`. Under the`di-check`feature, the macros emit`impl Provide<Self> for Wiring`for every component and a bound per concrete dependency, so a missing provider is a`cargo check`error.
- [Reloadable](https://docs.rs/trait.ReloadableConfig.html)- Config
- A config binding the reloader can re-bind: it knows its path, how to re-deserialize its
type from a re-read tree, and how to stage its current value. Object-safe so the
reloader holds a `Vec<Box<dyn ReloadableConfig>>`across all bound types.
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.Resolver.html)
- A source of resolved values of one kind (components, config, …).
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.ResolverCtx.html)- Ctx
- A type-keyed set of `Resolver`
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.ResolverCtxExt.html)- CtxExt
- Ergonomic, generic accessor over a `ResolverCtx``&dyn ResolverCtx`) gets`ctx.get_resolver::<R>()`for free.
- [Respond](https://docs.rs/trait.Respond.html)
- Sends the single response back to the caller of a unary inbound RPC.
- [Respond](https://docs.rs/trait.RespondStream.html)- Stream
- Converts a responder into a multi-item sink for server- and bidirectional-
streaming calls. Consuming the responder this way replaces the single
`respond`with a stream of items terminated by`finish`or`error`.
- [Response](https://docs.rs/trait.ResponseSink.html)- Sink
- The outbound half of a streaming call: many items followed by exactly one
terminator. `send`awaits when the peer is slow, providing backpressure.
- [Scope](https://docs.rs/trait.Scope.html)
- A lifetime scope label: where a component instance is stored and how long it lives.
- [Serve](https://docs.rs/trait.Serve.html)
- Serves a built protocol over a concrete endpoint type `E`. Kept separate from`Protocol``SocketAddr`. The serve loop only needs to watch`endpoint`and`shutdown`; lifecycle and reload are handled by the caller (`App::serve`).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/trait.ServiceComponent.html)- Component
- A `Component`
- [Static](https://docs.rs/trait.StaticScope.html)- Scope
- Ergonomic authoring sugar for a zero-sized scope: provide the three associated
constants and a `Scope``Connection`,`Request`, a custom`#[scope]`) declare themselves this way.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/trait.StreamDecode.html)- Decode
- The receive half of a stream item’s wire format: how frame bytes become an item.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/trait.StreamEncode.html)- Encode
- The send half of a stream item’s wire format: how an item becomes frame bytes.
- [Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html)
- An abstract source of inbound connections.
- [Wired](https://docs.rs/trait.Wired.html)
- Marker that all of a component’s dependencies are provided. Under `di-check`the macros emit`impl Wired for T where Wiring: Provide<Dep>, ..`carrying*every*single dependency (concrete and trait-object) as a lazy bound.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [dispatch_](https://docs.rs/fn.dispatch_factory.html)- factory
- Drives `factory`to a boxed component, erased to the`ComponentFactory`
- [factory_](https://docs.rs/fn.factory_dependencies.html)- dependencies
- The dependency edges of `factory`, recovered from its`Factory``Args`; the macro wraps a non-capturing call to this in the`fn() -> Vec<..>`the descriptor stores.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_boxed.html)- boxed
- Recovers handle `H`from a boxed slot: downcasts to its stored representation (`H::Stored`) and derives the handle. This is the single seam through which every resolution converts storage back into a handle — a snapshot for`Arc<T>`, a shared clone for`Dep<T>`, a plain clone for a by-value handle.`None`if the box holds a different stored type.
- [no_](https://docs.rs/fn.no_hooks.html)- hooks
- The empty hooks slice for a type that declares none — the default carried by a
`ComponentDescriptor`.
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_reload_triggers.html)- reload_ - triggers
- Spawns the background tasks for the requested triggers, returning their handles so the
caller can abort them on shutdown. Unsupported requests (SIGHUP off-Unix, watching
without the `watch`feature) are logged and skipped.
- [type_](https://docs.rs/fn.type_id_of.html)- id_ - of
- Returns the TypeId of T. Used as a function pointer in TypeDescriptor.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [CallId](https://docs.rs/type.CallId.html)
- Opaque identifier correlating a request to its response within a connection.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/type.ComponentContainer.html)- Container
- Backwards-compatible alias: the root singleton store is a `ScopeContainer`
- [Component](https://docs.rs/type.ComponentFactory.html)- Factory
- Async factory function pointer for constructing a component.
- [Dep](https://docs.rs/type.Dep.html)
- A reloadable dependency handle: a stable handle to a component slot whose instance may be swapped at runtime (e.g. by a config reload).
- [DiResult](https://docs.rs/type.DiResult.html)
- The DI layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated
**factory**code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/type.HookCall.html)- Call
- The erased call shape every hook is compiled to: resolve the receiver (if the method
takes `&self`) from the resolver context, extract the kind’s params from the erased context, run the method, and box its output. The boxed value is always the kind’s`Output`.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/type.HookResult.html)- Result
- The hook layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated hook
code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [component](https://docs.rs/attr.component.html)
- Declares a **system-constructed singleton component**on a struct.
- [config](https://docs.rs/attr.config.html)
- Implements the `ConfigProperties`trait for a config`struct`or`enum`, making it injectable as`Cfg<T>`from a property path.
- [injectable](https://docs.rs/attr.injectable.html)
- Marks a trait as injectable as `Arc<dyn Trait>`(providers register with`#[component(provide = dyn Trait)]`).
- [methods](https://docs.rs/attr.methods.html)
- Registers a component’s lifecycle methods from an inherent `impl`block.

# overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#overseerd)Overseerd

A component- and service-oriented framework. Depend on this single crate; it re-exports
the layered core — `overseerd-core` (vocabulary + resolver), `overseerd-di` (the DI
engine), `overseerd-hooks`, `overseerd-dirs`, `overseerd-config`, and `overseerd-app`
(the protocol-agnostic application core) — plus the procedural macros.

The native RPC daemon lives in its own `overseerd-rpc` crate and is re-exported here
behind the default-on ** daemon** feature (disable it with

`default-features = false`
for a core-framework-only build, or depend on `overseerd-rpc` directly).## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [builtins](https://docs.rs/builtins/index.html)
- Framework builtins: the seeded `ShutdownHandle``ServerConfig``LoggingConfig``init_tracing`subscriber helper.
- [client](https://docs.rs/client/index.html)
- The protocol-agnostic **client**core: the`ProtocolTransport``Client``app``daemon`, …) supplies a`ProtocolTransport`impl. Generated client code roots here, so it is identical across protocols.
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Config source-format markers for `ConfigManager<F>`:`Toml``Dynamic``yaml`feature)`Yaml`.
- [daemon](https://docs.rs/daemon/index.html)
- The native RPC **daemon**plugin surface, namespaced so plugin items never collide with the facade root or with other plugins (`overseerd::axum::*`, …).
- [dirs](https://docs.rs/dirs/index.html)
- Application directory kinds (`Config`,`Data`,`Cache`,`State`,`Runtime`,`Tmp`), the typed`Dir``DirectoriesManager``Dir<dirs::Config>`.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- The common imports for the **core framework**:`use overseerd::prelude::*;`. Pair with`use overseerd::daemon::prelude::*;`(or another plugin’s prelude) for the protocol layer.
- [scope](https://docs.rs/scope/index.html)
- Component lifetime scopes: the `Scope``#[component(scope = Request)]`; a`#[component]`defaults to`Singleton`
- [transport](https://docs.rs/transport/index.html)
- The full transport substrate, including the framing codec and connection/responder types for building custom transports.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [app](https://docs.rs/macro.app.html)
- Assembles an app and validates it from one declaration.
- [daemon](https://docs.rs/macro.daemon.html)
- Deprecated alias for `app!`

- [Directories](https://docs.rs/struct.DirectoriesManager.html)- Manager
- Resolves and hands out the application’s `Dir<K>`
- [Directories](https://docs.rs/struct.DirectoriesResolver.html)- Resolver
- A `config::Resolver``@`directory namespace.
- [Dynamic](https://docs.rs/struct.Dynamic.html)
- Field wrapper marking a dependency as **runtime-provided**.
- [Flags](https://docs.rs/struct.Flags.html)
- Combinable control-flow flags carried in the flags section of a
`StatusCode`
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Static metadata for one hook, registered into its type’s `{Type}Hooks`slice.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/struct.HookManager.html)- Manager
- Runs hooks of a kind against the live component instances.
- [Incoming](https://docs.rs/struct.IncomingCall.html)- Call
- An inbound RPC call received from the transport layer.
- [Live](https://docs.rs/struct.Live.html)
- A shared, swappable cell holding the current `Arc<T>`instance — the interior mutability primitive behind`Dep<T>``Cfg<T>`in the config layer).
- [LiveRef](https://docs.rs/struct.LiveRef.html)
- A guard pinning one generation of a `Live<T>``T`. Holding it keeps observing the generation current when`get``Live`, discouraging holding it across a long await (which would pin the old instance and delay a reload). Returned by both`Dep<T>``Cfg<T>`.
- [Logging](https://docs.rs/struct.LoggingConfig.html)- Config
- Tracing/logging settings consumed by the `init_tracing`helper, bound from a config subtree and injected as`Cfg<LoggingConfig>`
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryCall.html)- Call
- A client-side handle to one in-flight call, covering all four kinds: send inbound items (client/bidi), receive server events, and cancel.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryClient.html)- Client
- The client side of an in-memory transport. Primarily used in tests.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryConnection.html)- Connection
- A logical in-memory connection. Yielded by `MemoryTransport::accept`.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryConnectionHandle.html)- Connection - Handle
- A handle representing one logical connection on the client side. Dropped when the client is done with the connection.
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryResponder.html)- Responder
- Sends responses back through the call’s event channel (unary or streaming).
- [Memory](https://docs.rs/struct.MemoryTransport.html)- Transport
- The daemon side of an in-memory transport. Yields one `MemoryConnection`per`MemoryClient::connect`call.
- [Peer](https://docs.rs/struct.PeerInfo.html)- Info
- Transport-level information about the remote peer.
- [Provider](https://docs.rs/struct.ProviderDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Declares that a component **provides**a trait, so it can be injected as a single`Arc<dyn Trait>`(the primary or sole provider), or collected into a`Vec<Arc<dyn Trait>>`/`HashMap<String, Arc<dyn Trait>>`of all providers.
- [Reload](https://docs.rs/struct.ReloadProposal.html)- Proposal
- The proposed configuration handed to config-reload hooks: the staged value of every
binding (changed bindings hold their newly-deserialized value, unchanged bindings hold
their current value), so a hook’s `CfgNext<T>`
- [Reload](https://docs.rs/struct.ReloadTriggers.html)- Triggers
- Which automatic reload triggers a `ConfigManager``ConfigReloader::reload``serve`/`run`and spawns the matching background tasks.
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolverSet.html)- Set
- A type-keyed bag of `Resolver``ResolverCtx`
- [Scope](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)- Container
- One scope’s constructed instances, layered over an optional parent scope.
- [Server](https://docs.rs/struct.ServerConfig.html)- Config
- Network binding settings for a daemon’s transport, bound from a config subtree
and injected as `Cfg<ServerConfig>`
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.Shutdown.html)
- Fired once when the daemon begins a graceful shutdown (the serve/run loop has stopped).
Errors from a `#[hook(Shutdown)]`are logged; shutdown proceeds regardless.
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.ShutdownHandle.html)- Handle
- A cloneable handle for triggering graceful shutdown from any task.
- [Shutdown](https://docs.rs/struct.ShutdownSignal.html)- Signal
- Coordinates graceful daemon shutdown across all tasks in the process.
- [Startup](https://docs.rs/struct.Startup.html)
- Fired once after the daemon is built and before it begins serving. An `Err`from any`#[hook(Startup)]`aborts startup — the daemon does not begin accepting work.
- [Status](https://docs.rs/struct.StatusCode.html)- Code
- A structured status code carried on every error response.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamDecodeError.html)- Decode - Error
- A failure decoding a wire frame back into a stream item.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamEncodeError.html)- Encode - Error
- A failure encoding a stream item into a wire frame. Carries the `StatusCode`and body the terminating`StreamError`frame will report, mirroring the handler-side error currency so a custom codec can classify its own failures.
- [TcpTransport](https://docs.rs/struct.TcpTransport.html)
- TCP transport. Each accepted connection handles calls sequentially.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeDescriptor.html)- Descriptor
- Static metadata describing a Rust type, safe to embed in `'static`descriptors.
- [Unix](https://docs.rs/struct.UnixTransport.html)- Transport
- Unix socket transport. Removes the socket file on drop.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/struct.WireRequest.html)- Request
- The request half of the wire protocol, also the opening frame of a stream.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/struct.WireResponse.html)- Response
- The response half of the wire protocol.
- [Wiring](https://docs.rs/struct.Wiring.html)
- The crate-wide anchor that each component’s `Provide`impl attaches to. A dependency assertion is the bound`Wiring: Provide<Dep>`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.CallResult.html)- Result
- Success or failure of an RPC call at the transport layer.
- [Cardinality](https://docs.rs/enum.Cardinality.html)
- Cardinality of a dependency edge: how many values satisfy it.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigError.html)- Error
- Errors from loading, merging, and binding configuration.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/enum.ConfigReloadError.html)- Reload - Error
- Errors from a configuration reload. On any error the live values are left untouched — a reload commits only when every changed binding re-binds and every affected hook accepts.
- [Default](https://docs.rs/enum.DefaultSpec.html)- Spec
- The shape of a config type’s field defaults, emitted by the `#[config]`macro and consumed by the merge step.
- [DiError](https://docs.rs/enum.DiError.html)
- The DI layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated
**factory**code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`
- [EnumTag](https://docs.rs/enum.EnumTag.html)
- How an enum is tagged, so the merge can synthesize the same shape serde deserializes.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/enum.HookError.html)- Error
- The hook layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated hook
code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`*domain*outcome (e.g. whether a config reload is accepted) is its`HookKind::Output`
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/enum.HookOutcome.html)- Outcome
- What a `#[hook(ConfigReload)]`hook reports back.`Err`from the hook aborts the reload; these variants all mean the proposal was accepted.
- [Predefined](https://docs.rs/enum.PredefinedCode.html)- Code
- The framework-owned category occupying the predefined section of a
`StatusCode`
- [Server](https://docs.rs/enum.ServerEvent.html)- Event
- A server→client event for one call. Unary calls produce a single
`Response`; streaming calls produce`Item`s terminated by`End`or`Error`.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/enum.WireMessage.html)- Message
- Top-level wire message. Every frame on the wire is one of these.
- [Wire](https://docs.rs/enum.WireOutcome.html)- Outcome
- Success or failure at the wire level.

## Statics[§](https://docs.rs#statics)

- [COMPONENTS](https://docs.rs/static.COMPONENTS.html)
- Link-time registry of every discovered `ComponentDescriptor`
- [CONFIG_](https://docs.rs/static.CONFIG_BINDINGS.html)- BINDINGS
- Link-time registry of every auto-registered config binding (a `#[config(path = "..")]`type), collected by`ConfigManager::auto_discover`
- [PROVIDERS](https://docs.rs/static.PROVIDERS.html)
- Link-time registry of every discovered `ProviderDescriptor``provide = dyn Trait`). See`COMPONENTS`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.Component.html)
- Metadata trait for types registerable as components.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.ComponentFactories.html)- Factories
- A component type’s own construction factories.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/trait.ComponentHooks.html)- Hooks
- A component type’s own hooks.
- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.ConfigDefaults.html)- Defaults
- Runtime, object-safe access to a config type’s `DefaultSpec`
- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.ConfigProperties.html)- Properties
- A struct bindable from a configuration subtree, injectable as `Cfg<Self>`
- [Connection](https://docs.rs/trait.Connection.html)
- A live session between the daemon and one remote peer.
- [Container](https://docs.rs/trait.ContainerConfigExt.html)- Config - Ext
- Ad-hoc config access from a built container: the relocated `.config()`accessor.
- [Descriptor](https://docs.rs/trait.Descriptor.html)
- Connects a type to a static descriptor of kind `D`, enabling type-to-descriptor lookups where the type is known but its link-time descriptor would otherwise only be reachable through a slice.
- [DirKind](https://docs.rs/trait.DirKind.html)
- A kind of application directory. Implemented by the marker types and used by
`DirectoriesManager``Dir<Self>`
- [Factory](https://docs.rs/trait.Factory.html)
- An async factory function whose parameters are all `FromContainer``FactoryOutput``Args`is the parameter-tuple marker that selects the arity impl.
- [Factory](https://docs.rs/trait.FactoryOutput.html)- Output
- What a factory function may return: the component itself, or a `Result`of it.
- [From](https://docs.rs/trait.FromContainer.html)- Container
- A single factory parameter, resolvable from the construction context, that reports the dependency edge it represents.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/trait.HookKind.html)- Kind
- A kind of hook: the event a `#[hook(Kind)]`method reacts to.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/trait.HookParam.html)- Param
- A parameter a `#[hook(K)]`method may take: an input of kind`K`, extracted from the kind’s context — never a component dependency (those come through`&self`).
- [Injectable](https://docs.rs/trait.Injectable.html)
- How a resolved dependency is stored in, and handed out of, the container.
- [Plugin](https://docs.rs/trait.Plugin.html)
- A general extension unit applied to an app while it is built.
- [Protocol](https://docs.rs/trait.Protocol.html)
- A pluggable serve/dispatch layer over the app’s DI runtime. There is exactly one
active protocol per `App`.
- [Protocol](https://docs.rs/trait.ProtocolPlugin.html)- Plugin
- A `Plugin``Protocol``App`is built around exactly one of these.
- [Provide](https://docs.rs/trait.Provide.html)
- Compile-time dependency marker: `Wiring: Provide<T>`holds when some component in scope provides`T`. Under the`di-check`feature, the macros emit`impl Provide<Self> for Wiring`for every component and a bound per concrete dependency, so a missing provider is a`cargo check`error.
- [Reloadable](https://docs.rs/trait.ReloadableConfig.html)- Config
- A config binding the reloader can re-bind: it knows its path, how to re-deserialize its
type from a re-read tree, and how to stage its current value. Object-safe so the
reloader holds a `Vec<Box<dyn ReloadableConfig>>`across all bound types.
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.Resolver.html)
- A source of resolved values of one kind (components, config, …).
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.ResolverCtx.html)- Ctx
- A type-keyed set of `Resolver`
- [Resolver](https://docs.rs/trait.ResolverCtxExt.html)- CtxExt
- Ergonomic, generic accessor over a `ResolverCtx``&dyn ResolverCtx`) gets`ctx.get_resolver::<R>()`for free.
- [Respond](https://docs.rs/trait.Respond.html)
- Sends the single response back to the caller of a unary inbound RPC.
- [Respond](https://docs.rs/trait.RespondStream.html)- Stream
- Converts a responder into a multi-item sink for server- and bidirectional-
streaming calls. Consuming the responder this way replaces the single
`respond`with a stream of items terminated by`finish`or`error`.
- [Response](https://docs.rs/trait.ResponseSink.html)- Sink
- The outbound half of a streaming call: many items followed by exactly one
terminator. `send`awaits when the peer is slow, providing backpressure.
- [Scope](https://docs.rs/trait.Scope.html)
- A lifetime scope label: where a component instance is stored and how long it lives.
- [Serve](https://docs.rs/trait.Serve.html)
- Serves a built protocol over a concrete endpoint type `E`. Kept separate from`Protocol``SocketAddr`. The serve loop only needs to watch`endpoint`and`shutdown`; lifecycle and reload are handled by the caller (`App::serve`).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/trait.ServiceComponent.html)- Component
- A `Component`
- [Static](https://docs.rs/trait.StaticScope.html)- Scope
- Ergonomic authoring sugar for a zero-sized scope: provide the three associated
constants and a `Scope``Connection`,`Request`, a custom`#[scope]`) declare themselves this way.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/trait.StreamDecode.html)- Decode
- The receive half of a stream item’s wire format: how frame bytes become an item.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/trait.StreamEncode.html)- Encode
- The send half of a stream item’s wire format: how an item becomes frame bytes.
- [Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html)
- An abstract source of inbound connections.
- [Wired](https://docs.rs/trait.Wired.html)
- Marker that all of a component’s dependencies are provided. Under `di-check`the macros emit`impl Wired for T where Wiring: Provide<Dep>, ..`carrying*every*single dependency (concrete and trait-object) as a lazy bound.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [dispatch_](https://docs.rs/fn.dispatch_factory.html)- factory
- Drives `factory`to a boxed component, erased to the`ComponentFactory`
- [factory_](https://docs.rs/fn.factory_dependencies.html)- dependencies
- The dependency edges of `factory`, recovered from its`Factory``Args`; the macro wraps a non-capturing call to this in the`fn() -> Vec<..>`the descriptor stores.
- [from_](https://docs.rs/fn.from_boxed.html)- boxed
- Recovers handle `H`from a boxed slot: downcasts to its stored representation (`H::Stored`) and derives the handle. This is the single seam through which every resolution converts storage back into a handle — a snapshot for`Arc<T>`, a shared clone for`Dep<T>`, a plain clone for a by-value handle.`None`if the box holds a different stored type.
- [no_](https://docs.rs/fn.no_hooks.html)- hooks
- The empty hooks slice for a type that declares none — the default carried by a
`ComponentDescriptor`.
- [spawn_](https://docs.rs/fn.spawn_reload_triggers.html)- reload_ - triggers
- Spawns the background tasks for the requested triggers, returning their handles so the
caller can abort them on shutdown. Unsupported requests (SIGHUP off-Unix, watching
without the `watch`feature) are logged and skipped.
- [type_](https://docs.rs/fn.type_id_of.html)- id_ - of
- Returns the TypeId of T. Used as a function pointer in TypeDescriptor.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [CallId](https://docs.rs/type.CallId.html)
- Opaque identifier correlating a request to its response within a connection.
- [Component](https://docs.rs/type.ComponentContainer.html)- Container
- Backwards-compatible alias: the root singleton store is a `ScopeContainer`
- [Component](https://docs.rs/type.ComponentFactory.html)- Factory
- Async factory function pointer for constructing a component.
- [Dep](https://docs.rs/type.Dep.html)
- A reloadable dependency handle: a stable handle to a component slot whose instance may be swapped at runtime (e.g. by a config reload).
- [DiResult](https://docs.rs/type.DiResult.html)
- The DI layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated
**factory**code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/type.HookCall.html)- Call
- The erased call shape every hook is compiled to: resolve the receiver (if the method
takes `&self`) from the resolver context, extract the kind’s params from the erased context, run the method, and box its output. The boxed value is always the kind’s`Output`.
- [Hook](https://docs.rs/type.HookResult.html)- Result
- The hook layer’s own error/result, exposed under distinct names so macro-generated hook
code can name them without colliding with the root [`Error`]/`Result`

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [component](https://docs.rs/attr.component.html)
- Declares a **system-constructed singleton component**on a struct.
- [config](https://docs.rs/attr.config.html)
- Implements the `ConfigProperties`trait for a config`struct`or`enum`, making it injectable as`Cfg<T>`from a property path.
- [injectable](https://docs.rs/attr.injectable.html)
- Marks a trait as injectable as `Arc<dyn Trait>`(providers register with`#[component(provide = dyn Trait)]`).
- [methods](https://docs.rs/attr.methods.html)
- Registers a component’s lifecycle methods from an inherent `impl`block.

# overseerd/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # Overseerd
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! A component- and service-oriented framework. Depend on this single crate; it re-exports
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//! the layered core — `overseerd-core` (vocabulary + resolver), `overseerd-di` (the DI
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! engine), `overseerd-hooks`, `overseerd-dirs`, `overseerd-config`, and `overseerd-app`
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! (the protocol-agnostic application core) — plus the procedural macros.
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//!
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! The native RPC daemon lives in its own `overseerd-rpc` crate and is re-exported here
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! behind the default-on **`daemon`** feature (disable it with `default-features = false`
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! for a core-framework-only build, or depend on `overseerd-rpc` directly).

# overseerd::client - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/client/index.html

## Expand description

The protocol-agnostic **client** core: the [ ProtocolTransport](client::ProtocolTransport)
abstraction and the typed

[surface generated clients build on. Always available (like](client::Client)

`Client`[-layer items); a protocol (the RPC](https://docs.rs/macro.app.html)

`app``daemon`, …) supplies a
`ProtocolTransport` impl. Generated client code roots here, so it is identical across
protocols.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Codec](https://docs.rs/struct.CodecError.html)- Error
- A body encode/decode failure. Carries a `StatusCode``BadInput`) and a human-readable message.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.ErrorBody.html)- Body
- The client mirror of the server’s error response: a protocol-defined status `S`plus the raw error body bytes. The status is opaque to the framework (the protocol picks`S`; RPC uses its packed`transport::StatusCode`, HTTP uses`http::StatusCode`) — only the caller interprets it. The body is deserialized into`T`lazily and best-effort, so a body the handler serialized as a different type (or as raw, non-postcard bytes) degrades to a failed`deserialize`while`code`/`raw`stay usable.
- [Raw](https://docs.rs/struct.Raw.html)
- Marker for an error body whose payload type is not known statically (the generic call path). Typed clients substitute the method’s declared error type.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamArg.html)- Arg
- A boxed input stream a streaming-request capability accepts. Build one from any `Stream`with`.into()`(or`new`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Client](https://docs.rs/enum.ClientError.html)- Error
- Everything that can go wrong on a client call. Generic over the error body type `E`so typed clients surface an`ErrorBody<E>``deserialize``Raw`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Bidi](https://docs.rs/trait.BidiStreaming.html)- Streaming
- A bidirectional stream of requests and responses (HTTP/2, gRPC, custom RPC — *not*HTTP/1.1). The request stream is pumped concurrently with reading the response stream.
- [Client](https://docs.rs/trait.ClientStreaming.html)- Streaming
- A stream of requests, one response (HTTP/2, gRPC, custom RPC — *not*HTTP/1.1, which has no streamed request body, so it does not implement this trait).
- [Decodes](https://docs.rs/trait.Decodes.html)
- A protocol can decode a `T`(a request, response, or stream item) from a wire body.
- [Encodes](https://docs.rs/trait.Encodes.html)
- A protocol can encode a `T`(a request, response, or stream item) into a wire body. Implemented by a protocol for the message types it supports.
- [Server](https://docs.rs/trait.ServerStreaming.html)- Streaming
- One request, a stream of responses (HTTP/1.1 chunked/SSE, HTTP/2, gRPC, custom RPC). The
response stream is the protocol’s own type — a contract that the result *is*a`Stream`
- [Transport](https://docs.rs/trait.Transport.html)
- The base every capability shares: a transport carries a protocol-defined `Status``transport::StatusCode`; HTTP sets it to`http::StatusCode`. Every capability requires this, so a transport declares its status once and it threads through every call shape’s errors.
- [Unary](https://docs.rs/trait.Unary.html)
- One request, one response. Every protocol supports this. The implementation owns body
encoding (via `Encodes``Decodes`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [retype](https://docs.rs/fn.retype.html)
- Re-labels an untyped error onto a typed error of the same shape, preserving its status `S`. The only arm carrying`E`is`Remote`, whose body bytes are re-marked, not re-decoded. Used by protocol impls and generated clients.

# app in overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/macro.app.html

`app!() { /* proc-macro */ }`## Expand description

Assembles an app and validates it from one declaration.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// Built earlier in `main`, so their values can also configure the transport.
let config = ConfigManager::<Toml>::load_in(&dirs.dir(), &[])?;
let app = app! {
    name: "example-daemon",
    services: [Notifications, Echo],
    configs: [ DbConfig => "app.db.reader", DbConfig => "app.db.writer" ],
    managers: {
        config: config,        // hand in a pre-built `ConfigManager`
        directories: dirs,     // hand in a pre-built `DirectoriesManager`
    },
}
.build()
.await?;
```
Expands to an `AppBuilder` — `App::builder(name).auto_discover()`, a
`with_component(..)` for each listed instance, a `config::<T>(path)` for each
`configs` entry (`Type => "property.path"`), and `config_source`/`directories`
for any `managers` entries — so it is what you use in `main`.

- `configs`binds the same config type at several property paths; a type with a baked-in- `#[config(path = "..")]`auto-registers and needs no entry.
- `managers`hands in instances built earlier in- `main`:- `config: <binding>`a- `ConfigManager`- `directories: <binding>`a- `DirectoriesManager`- `Dir<Config>`directory, directories derived from the app name).

The listed `services` are additionally required to be
[ Wired](https://docs.rs/overseerd_core::Wired) under the

`di-check` feature, asserting their
whole dependency graph (including trait-object and `#[service]` field
dependencies, across crates) at compile time. The same declaration that wires the
app validates it — there is no separate list to maintain.

# overseerd::daemon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/daemon/index.html

## Expand description

The native RPC **daemon** plugin surface, namespaced so plugin items never collide with
the facade root or with other plugins (`overseerd::axum::*`, …).

Build an RPC app with `use overseerd::prelude::*;` (the core framework) plus
`use overseerd::daemon::prelude::*;` (the common RPC items). The daemon macros
(`#[service]`/`#[handlers]`/`#[rpc]`/`app!`) emit `::overseerd::daemon::*` paths, so end
users depend only on `overseerd` — never on `overseerd-rpc` directly.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use overseerd_rpc::`- [tower](https://docs.rs/tower/0.5.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tower/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Common imports for building an RPC daemon: `use overseerd::daemon::prelude::*;`(pair with the crate-root`use overseerd::prelude::*;`for the core framework +`app!`).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

Yields a [ &str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html) slice if the

`Path` is valid unicode.This conversion may entail doing a check for UTF-8 validity. Note that validation is performed because non-UTF-8 strings are perfectly valid for some OS.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```

let path = Path::new("foo.txt");

On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `c:\windows`is absolute, while`c:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use std::path::Path;
assert!(!Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the `Path` has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `c:\windows`but not`c:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use std::path::Path;
assert!(Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```
Returns the `Path` without its final component, if there is one.

This means it returns `Some("")` for relative paths with one component.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix, or if it’s
the empty string.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use std::path::Path;
let path = Path::new("/foo/bar");
let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(parent, Path::new("/foo"));
let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Path::new("/"));
assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
let relative_path = Path::new("foo/bar");
let parent = relative_path.parent();
assert_eq!(parent, Some(Path::new("foo")));
let grand_parent = parent.and_then(Path::parent);
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Some(Path::new("")));
let great_grand_parent = grand_parent.and_then(Path::parent);
assert_eq!(great_grand_parent, None);
```
Produces an iterator over `Path` and its ancestors.

The iterator will yield the `Path` that is returned if the [ parent](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.parent) method is used zero
or more times. If the

[method returns](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``Some(&self)`. Next it will yield
`&self.parent()`, `&self.parent().and_then(Path::parent)` and so on.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```

assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Path::new("..")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
```

If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it’s the path of a directory, this is the directory name.

`path_trailing_sep`)Checks whether the path ends in a trailing [separator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/constant.MAIN_SEPARATOR.html).

This is generally done to ensure that a path is treated as a directory, not a file, although it does not actually guarantee that such a path is a directory on the underlying file system.

Despite this behavior, two paths are still considered the same in Rust whether they have a trailing separator or not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```

assert!(Path::new("dir/").has_trailing_sep());
assert!(!Path::new("file.rs").has_trailing_sep());
```

Creates an owned [ PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html) with

`path` adjoined to `self`.If `path` is absolute, it replaces the current path.

On Windows:

- if `path`has a root but no prefix (e.g.,`\windows`), it replaces and returns everything except for the prefix (if any) of`self`.
- if `path`has a prefix but no root,`self`is ignored and`path`is returned.
- if `self`has a verbatim prefix (e.g.`\\?\C:\windows`) and`path`is not empty, the new path is normalized: all references to`.`and`..`are removed.

See [ PathBuf::push](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html#method.push) for more details on what it means to adjoin a path.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```

assert_eq!(Path::new("/etc").join("/bin/sh"), PathBuf::from("/bin/sh"));
```

1.0.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/std/path.rs.html#3244)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Components](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Components.html)<'_>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/std/path.rs.html#3244)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Components](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Components.html)<'_>

Produces an iterator over the [ Component](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/enum.Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
Trailing separators are normalized away, so `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-25)Examples

```
use std::path::{Path, Component};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
let mut components = Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Component::Normal(OsStr::new("tmp"))));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Component::Normal(OsStr::new("foo.txt"))));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ OsStr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/ffi/os_str/struct.OsStr.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-26)Examples

```
use std::path::{self, Path};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
let mut it = Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(OsStr::new(&path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string())));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(OsStr::new("tmp")));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(OsStr::new("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

`normalize_lexically`)Normalize a path, including `..` without traversing the filesystem.

Returns an error if normalization would leave leading `..` components.

This function always resolves `..` to the “lexical” parent.
That is “a/b/../c” will always resolve to `a/c` which can change the meaning of the path.
In particular, `a/c` and `a/b/../c` are distinct on many systems because `b` may be a symbolic link, so its parent isn’t `a`.

[ path::absolute](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/fn.absolute.html) is an alternative that preserves

`..`.
Or [can be used to resolve any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.canonicalize)

`Path::canonicalize``..` by querying the filesystem.Reads a symbolic link, returning the file that the link points to.

This is an alias to [ fs::read_link](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.read_link.html).

1.63.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/std/path.rs.html#3580)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

[ Path::exists()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.exists) only checks whether or not a path was both found and readable. By
contrast,

`try_exists` will return `Ok(true)` or `Ok(false)`, respectively, if the path
was *verified*to exist or not exist. If its existence can neither be confirmed nor denied, it will propagate an

`Err(_)` instead. This can be the case if e.g. listing
permission is denied on one of the parent directories.Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use ([TOCTOU](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/index.html#time-of-check-to-time-of-use-toctou)) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

This is an alias for [ std::fs::exists](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.exists.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```

assert!(!Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").try_exists().expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt"));
assert!(Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```

# DirectoriesManager in overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/struct.DirectoriesManager.html

`pub struct DirectoriesManager { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Resolves and hands out the application’s [ Dir<K>](https://docs.rs/struct.Dir.html) directories.

Built once (in `main` or by the daemon builder) from project metadata; cloneable
and injectable, so components can resolve arbitrary directory kinds on demand.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

A best-effort manager for `application`: platform project dirs when available,
otherwise a layout rooted under the system temp directory. Never fails.

Every known directory kind as a `(label, resolved path)` pair, in a stable order.

This is the directory namespace as plain data: the config crate inspects it to build
a `${@<label>}` templating resolver, so config never names the individual `Dir` kind
types — only this list. Labels are the [ DirKind::LABEL](https://docs.rs/trait.DirKind.html#associatedconstant.LABEL)s:

`config`, `data`, `cache`,
`state`, `runtime`, `tmp`.## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# overseerd::scope - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/scope/index.html

## Expand description

Component lifetime scopes: the [ Scope](https://docs.rs/trait.Scope.html) trait a protocol’s scope chain is built from,
plus the marker types. A component selects one with

`#[component(scope = Request)]`; a
`#[component]` defaults to [.](https://docs.rs/struct.Singleton.html)

`Singleton`The core defines only the universal anchors [ Singleton](https://docs.rs/struct.Singleton.html) and

[;](https://docs.rs/struct.Transient.html)

`Transient``Connection` and `Request` are RPC-protocol scopes from
`overseerd-rpc`, available with the `daemon` feature.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Connection](https://docs.rs/struct.Connection.html)
- A per-connection scope: a live session between the daemon and one remote peer.
Outlives the requests multiplexed over it, so it ranks above `Request`
- [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.Request.html)
- A per-request scope: one inbound RPC call.
- [Singleton](https://docs.rs/struct.Singleton.html)
- The root scope: a single instance for the whole application lifetime. The
longest-lived scope there can be, so it ranks `u8::MAX`
- [Transient](https://docs.rs/struct.Transient.html)
- A transient scope: rebuilt fresh on every resolution and never cached. The
shortest-lived scope there can be, so it ranks `u8::MIN`

---

Serves the app’s protocol over `endpoint` until ctrl-c or a shutdown signal.

The agnostic envelope: runs startup hooks, spawns config-reload triggers, bridges
ctrl-c to the shutdown signal, then hands the runtime + shutdown signal to the
protocol’s [ Serve](https://docs.rs/trait.Serve.html) impl. Shutdown hooks run on the way out.

# AppBuilder in overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/struct.AppBuilder.html

`pub struct AppBuilder<P>{ /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Assembles an [ App](https://docs.rs/struct.App.html) from an explicit set of components and the protocol plugin.

Generic over the [ ProtocolPlugin](https://docs.rs/trait.ProtocolPlugin.html) it installs. The agnostic builder methods (config,
components, directories, auto-discovery) live here; protocol-specific methods come from
an extension trait (e.g.

`RpcAppBuilder` in `overseerd-rpc`), so the same builder serves
any protocol.## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# AppRegistry in overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/struct.AppRegistry.html

```
pub struct AppRegistry {
    pub components:
```
[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ComponentDescriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentDescriptor.html)>,
    pub providers: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ProviderDescriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.ProviderDescriptor.html)>,
    pub config_bindings: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ConfigBinding](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigBinding.html)>,
}## Expand description

Holds the *agnostic* component, provider, and config-binding descriptors of an app —
declarations only. Runtime instances live in the
[ ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html).

Wraps the DI engine’s [ ComponentRegistry](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentRegistry.html) (component/provider graph) with the config
bindings, and runs the cross-cutting validation the component graph alone cannot
(config edges). Protocol-specific declarations (services/routes) live in the protocol
plugin, not here, so this stays usable by any protocol.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

`config_bindings: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[ConfigBinding](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfigBinding.html)>Config bindings (a config type bound to a property path). Populated from the auto-discovered config bindings slice and from explicit builder bindings.

# ScopeContainer in overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/struct.ScopeContainer.html

`pub struct ScopeContainer { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

One scope’s constructed instances, layered over an optional parent scope.

The root container is the singleton scope (`parent: None`); a per-connection
scope parents the root, and a per-request scope parents the connection.
Resolution walks this scope first, then each longer-lived parent, so a request
handler sees request-, connection-, and singleton-scoped instances uniformly.

The container is also a [ ResolverCtx](https://docs.rs/trait.ResolverCtx.html): it exposes a

[(for resolving components by type — used by hooks and config-targeted resolution) plus any](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentSource.html)

`ComponentSource`*external*resolvers (the config store) threaded in at build.

Resolves all registered singleton components in dependency order into the root container.

`components` is the singleton-scoped component set (after default/override
resolution). `instances` holds pre-built singletons supplied at the builder;
they are seeded first, so factory-built components may depend on them.
`externals` is the external resolver set (e.g. the config store) the factories
resolve `Cfg<T>` and similar through.

[Source](https://docs.rs/overseerd-di/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/overseerd_di/container.rs.html#180-186)#### pub async fn [open_child](https://docs.rs#method.open_child)(

#### pub async fn [open_child](https://docs.rs#method.open_child)(
    scope: &'static dyn [Scope](https://docs.rs/trait.Scope.html),
    parent: [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)>,
    registry: [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeRegistry](https://docs.rs/overseerd-di/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_di/container/struct.ScopeRegistry.html)>,
    order: &[[ComponentDescriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.ComponentDescriptor.html)],
    seeds: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[BoxedComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.BoxedComponent.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)>, [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.DiError.html)>

Opens a child scope over `parent`, seeding `seeds` then constructing `order`
(a dependency order precomputed at application build). Every scope — the four
built-ins and any future user-defined one — is created through this single
primitive.

An **empty** scope (nothing to construct, nothing to seed) holds no state of
its own, so resolution through it would only pass through to `parent`. Rather
than allocate a redundant container, this returns `parent` directly.

Returns the registered component of type `T` as its handle (`Arc<T>` by
default, or the by-value handle for a `#[component(by_value)]` type),
resolved through this scope and its parents.

[Source](https://docs.rs/overseerd-di/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/overseerd_di/container.rs.html#271)#### pub async fn [resolve](https://docs.rs#method.resolve)<H>(self: &[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)>) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<H>

[Source](https://docs.rs/overseerd-di/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/overseerd_di/container.rs.html#271)

#### pub async fn [resolve](https://docs.rs#method.resolve)<H>(self: &[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)>) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<H>

Resolves `H` through this scope then each parent, or — if `H::Target` is a
`Transient` — constructs a fresh instance.

Extracts any [ FromContainer](https://docs.rs/trait.FromContainer.html) value from this scope — the
request-time analogue of a factory parameter.

Views the scope as a construction context parented at itself, so the *whole*
`FromContainer` set resolves the same way a constructor’s parameters do: components
(`Arc<T>`, `Dep<T>`, by-value injectables, and `Vec`/`HashMap`/`Option` of providers)
through the scope chain, and resolver-backed values (`Cfg<T>`, and any future
resolver-sourced type) through the threaded resolvers. A protocol’s `Inject` extractor
builds on this, so a handler can inject anything a constructor can — not just the
`Injectable` subset that [ resolve](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html#method.resolve) covers.

# AppRuntime in overseerd - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/overseerd/0.9.0/overseerd/struct.AppRuntime.html

`pub struct AppRuntime { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Everything a protocol needs to drive requests through DI, cheaply cloneable.

Agnostic to any particular protocol: it holds the built root scope, the per-scope
construction orders keyed by scope name (computed from the protocol’s declared
scope chain), the resolved component set, and the hook manager. A protocol opens
its scopes through [ open_scope](https://docs.rs/struct.AppRuntime.html#method.open_scope), naming each scope from its own
chain.

#### pub async fn [open_scope](https://docs.rs#method.open_scope)(
    &self,
    scope: &'static dyn [Scope](https://docs.rs/trait.Scope.html),
    parent: [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)>,
    seeds: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[BoxedComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.BoxedComponent.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[ScopeContainer](https://docs.rs/struct.ScopeContainer.html)>, [Error](https://docs.rs/overseerd-app/0.9.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/overseerd_app/error/enum.Error.html)>

Opens a child container for `scope` over `parent`, seeding `seeds` and
constructing that scope’s precomputed order (empty when the scope holds nothing
constructable). An empty, unseeded scope is skipped — `parent` is returned
unchanged. `scope` must be one the app was built for (in the protocol’s chain).

[TypeDescriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeDescriptor.html),
    pub value: [Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)<dyn [Any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html) + [Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + [Sync](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)>,
}## Expand description

A type-erased instantiated component.

`value` stores `Arc<T>` inside a `Box<dyn Any + Send + Sync>`, which
allows recovery via `value.downcast_ref::<Arc<T>>()`.
